cases.sentence: Он указал на ___.
cases.explain: «другого помещика» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: He indicated the other landowner.

cases.sentence: Это разве ___? – сказал помещик, очевидно щеголяя словом «рациональное».
cases.explain: «рациональное хозяйство» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, the thing’s done at Mihail Petrovitch’s, but ask him how it’s done. Do you call that a rational system?” said the landowner, obviously rather proud of the word “rational.”

cases.sentence: Мое хозяйство все, чтобы денежки к ___ были готовы.
cases.explain: «осенним податям» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “My system’s very simple,” said Mihail Petrovitch, “thank God. All my management rests on getting the money ready for the autumn taxes, and the peasants come to me, ‘Father, master, help us!’ Well, the peasants are all one’s neighbors; one feels for them. So one advances them a third, but one says: ‘Remember, lads, I have helped you, and you must help me when I need it—whether it’s the sowing of the oats, or the haycutting, or the harvest’; and well, one agrees, so much for each taxpayer—though there are dishonest ones among them too, it’s true.”

cases.sentence: Левин, зная давно эти патриархальные приемы, переглянулся с Свияжским и перебил Михаила Петровича, обращаясь опять к помещику с ___.
cases.explain: «седыми усами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Levin, who had long been familiar with these patriarchal methods, exchanged glances with Sviazhsky and interrupted Mihail Petrovitch, turning again to the gentleman with the gray whiskers.

cases.sentence: – Да так же и вести, как Михаил Петрович: – или отдать исполу, или внаймы мужикам; это можно, но только этим самым уничтожается ___ государства.
cases.explain: «общее богатство» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Why, manage like Mihail Petrovitch, or let the land for half the crop or for rent to the peasants; that one can do—only that’s just how the general prosperity of the country is being ruined. Where the land with serf-labor and good management gave a yield of nine to one, on the half-crop system it yields three to one. Russia has been ruined by the emancipation!”

cases.sentence: Где земля у меня при ___ и хорошем хозяйстве приносила сам-девять, она исполу принесет самтретей.
cases.explain: «крепостном труде» — after the preposition «при», for location or topic.

Where the land with serf-labor and good management gave a yield of nine to one, on the half-crop system it yields three to one. Russia has been ruined by the emancipation!”

cases.sentence: Теперь-с, при уничтожении ___, у нас отняли власть, и хозяйство наше, то, где оно поднято на высокий уровень, должно опуститься к самому дикому, первобытному состоянию.
cases.explain: «крепостного права» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “The point is, don’t you see, that progress of every sort is only made by the use of authority,” he said, evidently wishing to show he was not without culture. “Take the reforms of Peter, of Catherine, of Alexander. Take European history. And progress in agriculture more than anything else—the potato, for instance, that was introduced among us by force. The wooden plough too wasn’t always used. It was introduced maybe in the days before the Empire, but it was probably brought in by force. Now, in our own day, we landowners in the serf times used various improvements in our husbandry: drying machines and thrashing machines, and carting manure and all the modern implements—all that we brought into use by our authority, and the peasants opposed it at first, and ended by imitating us. Now, by the abolition of serfdom we have been deprived of our authority; and so our husbandry, where it had been raised to a high level, is bound to sink to the most savage primitive condition. That’s how I see it.”

cases.sentence: Теперь-с, при уничтожении крепостного права, у нас отняли власть, и хозяйство наше, то, где оно поднято на ___, должно опуститься к самому дикому, первобытному состоянию.
cases.explain: «высокий уровень» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.

Now, by the abolition of serfdom we have been deprived of our authority; and so our husbandry, where it had been raised to a high level, is bound to sink to the most savage primitive condition. That’s how I see it.”

cases.sentence: «Вот она – ___, главный элемент хозяйства», – подумал Левин.
cases.explain: «рабочая сила» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “There it is—the labor force—the chief element in agriculture,” thought Levin.

cases.sentence: «Вот она – рабочая сила, ___ хозяйства», – подумал Левин.
cases.explain: «главный элемент» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “There it is—the labor force—the chief element in agriculture,” thought Levin.

cases.sentence: – Рабочие не хотят работать хорошо и работать ___.
cases.explain: «хорошими орудиями» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “The laborers won’t work well, and won’t work with good implements. Our laborer can do nothing but get drunk like a pig, and when he’s drunk he ruins everything you give him. He makes the horses ill with too much water, cuts good harness, barters the tires of the wheels for drink, drops bits of iron into the thrashing machine, so as to break it. He loathes the sight of anything that’s not after his fashion. And that’s how it is the whole level of husbandry has fallen. Lands gone out of cultivation, overgrown with weeds, or divided among the peasants, and where millions of bushels were raised you get a hundred thousand; the wealth of the country has decreased. If the same thing had been done, but with care that. …”

cases.sentence: Земли заброшены, заросли полынями или розданы мужикам, и где производили миллион, производят сотни тысяч четвертей; ___ уменьшилось.
cases.explain: «общее богатство» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: – Я не нахожу, – уже серьезно возразил Свияжский, – я только вижу то, что мы не умеем вести хозяйство и что, напротив, то хозяйство, которое мы вели при ___, не то что слишком высоко, а слишком низко.
cases.explain: «крепостном праве» — after the preposition «при», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “I don’t believe it,” Sviazhsky replied quite seriously; “all I see is that we don’t know how to cultivate the land, and that our system of agriculture in the serf days was by no means too high, but too low. We have no machines, no good stock, no efficient supervision; we don’t even know how to keep accounts. Ask any landowner; he won’t be able to tell you what crop’s profitable, and what’s not.”

cases.sentence: Дрянную молотилку, ___ ваш, сломают, а мою паровую не сломают.
cases.explain: «российский топчачок» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Why do they spoil things? A poor thrashing machine, or your Russian presser, they will break, but my steam press they don’t break. A wretched Russian nag they’ll ruin, but keep good dray-horses—they won’t ruin them. And so it is all round. We must raise our farming to a higher level.”

cases.sentence: – Вот это верно, – засмеявшись даже от удовольствия, подтвердил помещик с ___.
cases.explain: «седыми усами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “That’s true enough,” the gentleman with the gray whiskers chimed in, positively laughing with satisfaction.

cases.sentence: – И я не один, – продолжал Левин, – я сошлюсь на всех хозяев, ведущих рационально дело; все, за ___, ведут дело в убыток.
cases.explain: «редкими исключениями» — after the preposition «за», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “And I’m not the only one,” pursued Levin. “I mix with all the neighboring landowners, who are cultivating their land on a rational system; they all, with rare exceptions, are doing so at a loss. Come, tell us how does your land do—does it pay?” said Levin, and at once in Sviazhsky’s eyes he detected that fleeting expression of alarm which he had noticed whenever he had tried to penetrate beyond the outer chambers of Sviazhsky’s mind.

cases.sentence: – Может быть, невыгодно, – отвечал Свияжский. – Это только доказывает, или что я ___, или что я затрачиваю капитал на увеличение ренты.
cases.explain: «плохой хозяин» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Possibly it does not pay,” answered Sviazhsky. “That merely proves either that I’m a bad manager, or that I’ve sunk my capital for the increase of my rents.”

cases.sentence: И в самом ___ духа Свияжский встал и отошел, видимо предполагая, что разговор окончен на том самом месте, где Левину казалось, что он только начинается.
cases.explain: «приятном расположении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: And in the happiest frame of mind Sviazhsky got up and walked off, apparently supposing the conversation to have ended at the very point when to Levin it seemed that it was only just beginning.

cases.sentence: И в самом приятном расположении духа Свияжский встал и отошел, видимо предполагая, что разговор окончен на том ___, где Левину казалось, что он только начинается.

cases.sentence: – Отчего вы думаете, – говорил Левин, стараясь вернуться к вопросу, – что нельзя найти такого отношения к ___, при которой работа была бы производительна?
cases.explain: «рабочей силе» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “What makes you think,” said Levin, trying to get back to the question, “that it’s impossible to find some relation to the laborer in which the labor would become productive?”

cases.sentence: – Никогда этого с ___ не будет!
cases.explain: «русским народом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “That never could be so with the Russian peasantry; we’ve no power over them,” answered the landowner.

cases.sentence: – Потому что это все равно, что придумывать вновь приемы для постройки ___.
cases.explain: «железных дорог» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Because it would be just like inventing afresh the means for constructing railways. They are ready, invented.”

cases.sentence: Потом вся эта ___ рабочего вопроса, самого либерального лассалевского направления…
cases.explain: «громадная литература» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “That question is now absorbing the best minds in Europe. The Schulze-Delitsch movement. … And then all this enormous literature of the labor question, the most liberal Lassalle movement … the Mulhausen experiment? That’s a fact by now, as you’re probably aware.”

cases.sentence: Я, разумеется, не ___, но меня это интересовало, и, право, если вас интересует, вы займитесь.

cases.translation: “No, you only say that; no doubt you know all about it as well as I do. I’m not a professor of sociology, of course, but it interested me, and really, if it interests you, you ought to study it.”

cases.sentence: Помещики встали, и Свияжский, опять остановив Левина в его ___ заглядывать в то, что сзади приемных комнат его ума, пошел провожать своих гостей.
cases.explain: «неприятной привычке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The two neighbors had risen, and Sviazhsky, once more checking Levin in his inconvenient habit of peeping into what was beyond the outer chambers of his mind, went to see his guests out.
